title: The Deadmines
body: The Deadmines lie beneath Moonbrook in southern Westfall. Once the greatest source of gold in the human lands, their dark tunnels are now the private sanctum of the Defias Brotherhood, and its master, Edwin VanCleef, keeps to the deepest part of them. Defias miners still work the rock under the eye of overseers, evokers and taskmasters, and an ogre foreman holds the first chamber. Goblins labor here as well, cutting timber and smelting ore, and it is rumored that the Brotherhood has set them to build something at the bottom of the mines, though what it may be no one outside can say. Few outsiders come here by choice. The People's Militia wants the Brotherhood's highest ranks cut down, a gnome in Stormwind wants a goblin shredder that still works somewhere in the depths, and a dwarf in Stormwind still hopes for word of the miners lost when a tunnel came down on them.

parts.body: Not every Defias miner is nameless. One called Miner Johnson is sometimes found at work in the tunnels, though often he is nowhere to be seen. Where he does stand, he fights harder than the diggers around him, his blows tearing through armor, until he too falls among the rock he was cutting.

title: Ironclad Cove
body: At the bottom of the Deadmines a heavy iron-clad door shuts off Ironclad Cove, a great sea cavern hidden from the world above. Here is what the goblins have been building toward: a great ship, fitted out at docks and scaffolding while goblin shipbuilders swarm over her. Defias pirates crew her, squallshapers wielding fire and frost stand among them, and blackguards wait unseen in the shadows. Before the door stand a Defias cannon and a store of the Brotherhood's own gunpowder. Aboard her waits the master of the Brotherhood himself.

parts.body: The ship's captain, the goblin Captain Greenskin, kept watch from her upper deck with his crew around him. He fought with a cleaving blade and a harpoon whose barb carried poison into the wound, but the deck he commanded was where he fell.

title: Rhahk'Zor
body: Rhahk'Zor, called the Foreman, is an ogre who keeps the first great chamber of the Deadmines for the Defias Brotherhood. Defias miners work the rock around him, two Defias watchmen stand at his side, and behind him a heavy door bars the way into the deeper mine. He wears no red bandana, but he serves the Brotherhood all the same, and while he stands before the door it stays shut.

parts.body: Rhahk'Zor greeted intruders with a promise: VanCleef pay big for you heads. He swung slams that left them stunned and reeling, but the bounty went unclaimed. When the ogre fell, the heavy door at his back swung open on the deeper workings of the mine.

title: Sneed
body: Sneed, the Lumbermaster, is a goblin who keeps the Brotherhood's timber works in the Mast Room, deep in the Deadmines, where goblin woodcarvers cut and shape timber. He does not work with his own hands. Sneed sits in the cockpit of a goblin shredder, a towering logging machine, and from inside it he watches over the woodcarvers and meets anyone who troubles them. A heavy door at the far end of his workshop stays shut while he holds it.

parts.body: Sneed's shredder fought as hard as any guard in the mine. It struck terror into its foes, sending them fleeing, and wracked spellcasters with pain that slowed their casting. When the machine was finally broken, it threw Sneed out of the cockpit, and the goblin came on afoot.

parts.body: Out of his machine, Sneed fought to tear the weapons from his attackers' hands, but he fell beside the wreck of his shredder. With the Lumbermaster dead, the door of the Mast Room opened on the way deeper into the mine.

title: Gilnid
body: Gilnid, the Smelter, is a goblin who runs the Goblin Foundry deep in the Deadmines. Goblin craftsmen melt ore at its furnaces, goblin engineers stand ready with remote-controlled golems, and a Defias taskmaster keeps watch among them. Gilnid does not let the work slacken. Every so often his voice carries across the foundry, ordering the parts moved down to the ship, or asking whether anyone wants a break, only to tell his oafs that it is too bad and to get back to work.

parts.body: Gilnid fought among his furnaces, splashing his attackers with molten metal that burned them and slowed their every move. The smelter fell all the same, and as he died the heavy foundry door opened on the way deeper into the mine.

title: Mr. Smite
body: Mr. Smite, a tauren, is first mate of the Brotherhood's ship in Ironclad Cove, and he guards the way to her. He keeps an ear on the iron-clad door that shuts off the cove. Should anyone blast it open with the cannon that stands before it, Smite hears the noise at once and sends his men to look, and moments later he cries the alarm across the cove: the ship is under attack, and the crew must repel the invaders.

parts.body: Smite met his attackers with a single blade. Hard pressed, he stamped so hard that all around him reeled, called them tougher landlubbers than he had thought, and knelt to take up a second blade. Pressed again, he roared that now they were making him angry and came back with a great hammer. It was not enough, and the first mate fell at his post.

title: The Collapsed Tunnel
body: In Stormwind the dwarf Wilder Thistlenettle tells of the day the mine turned on him. He and his crew were deep in a vast mine hidden beneath a barn in Moonbrook, with thieves appearing from nowhere around them, when the tunnel collapsed. Wilder got out. The others, among them his brother the foreman, were never heard from again. He asks anyone bound for the mine to look for his brother, or at least for the Explorers' League badge his brother always carried, and to bring back any Miners' Union cards found there, so that the families of his lost friends can have some resolution.

parts.body: The miners had not stayed buried. In the collapsed wing of the tunnels the dead had risen again as skeletal miners, excavators and dynamiters, and their union cards were taken from them. Wilder thanked the one who brought them back and promised to see the families told, so that the dead might find some peace.
sources: quest 168 description and reward text (help bring peace to the dead; the families notified)

parts.body: Foreman Thistlenettle was found at last. He walked the collapsed tunnels with the rest of his dead crew, no longer a living man, and his Explorers' League badge came back from his body. Wilder had feared as much. He thanked the one who brought it for ending the mystery, grim as its ending was.
sources: quest 167 completion and reward text (Is there any hope after all this time?; My suspicions were correct. My poor brother; some conclusion to this mystery, even if the conclusion was grim)

title: Red Silk Bandanas
body: The red bandana is the trademark of the Defias Brotherhood, but Scout Riell of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill has learned that it tells more than membership. The cloth a member's bandana is made of shows his rank. Riell wants as many of the Brotherhood's high ranking members cut down as can be managed, and the highest of them, she is sure, will be found in VanCleef's secret hideout. Ten red silk bandanas will serve as proof of their deaths.

parts.body: The silk came back to Sentinel Hill, ten red bandanas taken from the Brotherhood's dead. Riell saluted the one who brought them on behalf of the People's Militia. With help from brave souls like these, she said, the land would soon be returned to its people.

title: Underground Assault
body: Gnomeregan has fallen to the troggs, and Shoni the Shilent, a gnome in Stormwind, means to break back in from below. Her gyrodrillmatic excavationators could bore through the rocky borders of the city and open the way for a gnomish assault, if only they had the power. Shoni knows where to find it. Deep in the Deadmines, she has heard, a goblin shredder is still working, and its power supply, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket, would serve her drills, if someone can find the machine and bring the part back intact.

parts.body: The Gnoam Sprecklesprocket reached Stormwind intact, pulled from the wreck of the shredder that Sneed the Lumbermaster had ridden. Shoni was delighted. Thanks to it, she said, Gnomeregan was one step closer to its day of liberation.
